Norovirus Outbreak Disrupts New Zealand Telecom Operations

A norovirus outbreak affecting several telecommunications sites across New Zealand has caused significant workforce shortages and service delays, with industry leaders warning of continued disruption as the situation unfolds.

The outbreak, first detected last week at a central Auckland operations centre, has since been confirmed at multiple customer service and network maintenance facilities, according to the New Zealand Telecommunications Association (NZTA). As of Tuesday, more than 110 employees from three major telecom companies—including CoreConnect NZ, Pacific FibreLink, and Wavelength Telecom—were reported to be on medical leave following norovirus infection.

"This is a challenging situation for our sector," said NZTA spokesperson Moana Reilly. "Our members are seeing up to 30% absenteeism at affected sites, particularly among field technicians and call centre staff. This inevitably impacts scheduled network upgrades and fault repairs."

The Ministry of Health is working with telecom companies to contain the outbreak, recommending increased sanitation, staggered shifts, and temporary closure of break rooms. Several network maintenance projects in the Waikato and Wellington regions have been postponed, and customers have reported wait times of up to 72 hours for fault restoration.

"The health and safety of our team is our top priority," said Iain Roberts, HR Director at CoreConnect NZ. "We're deploying remote service tools and redirecting calls where possible, but some delays are unavoidable."

Industry analysts forecast ongoing disruptions if absentee rates do not decline within the coming week. "The industry’s resilience is being tested," said Rena Patel, a telecom sector analyst. "Contingency plans are in place, but prolonged staff shortages could impact both urban and rural connectivity."
